title: Congratulations to Jimmy Tsang on Successfully Defending His Thesis
summary: Jimmy Tsang successfully defended his thesis, 'Smart Grid Power Forecasting: An Investigation Into Graph Attention-Enhanced Temporal Fusion Transformer for Short Term Load Forecasting,' on September 1, 2026.
content:
Thesis Defense Success!

Congratulations to Jimmy Tsang on the successful defense of his thesis, 'Smart Grid Power Forecasting: An Investigation Into Graph Attention-Enhanced Temporal Fusion Transformer for Short Term Load Forecasting,' held on Tuesday, September 1, 2026.

The defense was supervised by Dr. Thangarajah Akilan

Jimmy's thesis proposes a novel approach integrating a Temporal Fusion Transformer (TFT) with a Graph Attention Network (GAT) to improve short-term load forecasting for smart grids, capturing cross-feature relationships that traditional TFT models miss. Trained and evaluated on the IESO, ENTSOE, AEP, and ELIA datasets, the model achieved state-of-the-art or near state-of-the-art performance, including a MAPE of 2.92% and 2.18% on Ontario and market demand forecasting, respectively.

Well done, Jimmy! We look forward to seeing the continued impact of your research on smart grid forecasting.

title: Congratulations to Kenneth Shahi and Joiebdeep Singh on Completing Their NSERC USRA Projects
summary: Kenneth Shahi and Joiebdeep Singh successfully completed their NSERC Undergraduate Student Research Award projects and presented their findings at VIDLab on August 13, 2026.
content:
NSERC USRA Project Presentations

Congratulations to Kenneth Shahi and Joiebdeep Singh on the successful completion of their NSERC Undergraduate Student Research Award (USRA) projects! On August 13, 2026, both students presented their research findings to the VIDLab team, capping off a summer of dedicated research work.

Project Highlights:

  • Kenneth Shahi: 'A Deep Learning Approach for Enhancing Low-Resolution PET Brain Scans' — developing deep learning techniques to improve the resolution and diagnostic quality of PET brain imaging.
  • Joiebdeep Singh: 'Drone-Based AI-Driven Parking Pass Detection and Enforcement System' — building an AI-powered drone system for automated detection and enforcement of parking permits.

Their work reflects strong initiative and research potential, and we are proud of the progress both students made during their NSERC USRA terms.

Kenneth and Joiebdeep presenting their NSERC USRA research

Well done, Kenneth and Joiebdeep! We look forward to seeing where your research journeys take you next.

title: Congratulations to Chee Mei Ling (Irene) on Journal Acceptance in Applied Soft Computing
summary: Congratulations to Chee Mei Ling (Irene), Thangarajah Akilan, Aparna Ravindra Phalke, and Kanchan Keisham for the acceptance of their paper 'DAS-SK: An Adaptive Model Integrating Dual Atrous Separable and Selective Kernel CNN for Agriculture Semantic Segmentation' in Applied Soft Computing.
content:
Journal Paper Acceptance!

We are delighted to congratulate Chee Mei Ling (Irene), Thangarajah Akilan, Aparna Ravindra Phalke, and Kanchan Keisham on the acceptance of their paper titled 'DAS-SK: An Adaptive Model Integrating Dual Atrous Separable and Selective Kernel CNN for Agriculture Semantic Segmentation' for publication in Applied Soft Computing, a leading Elsevier journal.

This work builds on the team's earlier research on dual atrous separable convolution for agricultural semantic segmentation, extending it with an adaptive selective kernel CNN architecture that further improves segmentation performance for agricultural imagery.

Congratulations, Irene, on this outstanding achievement! This is a fantastic milestone in your research journey, and we look forward to celebrating your continued success.

title: Congratulations to Our 2026 Graduates - Gaeul Han and Ebenezer Penoo

content:
Celebrating Academic Excellence and Research Achievements at 2026 Convocation!

Graduate Achievements:

  • Gaeul Han: Completed her MSc in Electrical and Computer Engineering with groundbreaking research on thermal image object detection. Her work on spatial edge-aware attention and self-supervision methods advances autonomous driving and low-visibility perception systems. Gaeul successfully presented her research at the 39th Canadian Conference on Artificial Intelligence (Canadian AI 2026).
  • Ebenezer Penoo: Achieved his MSc in Electrical and Computer Engineering with innovative research on intelligent transportation systems. His work on attention-gated bidirectional LSTM for real-time rear-end collision prediction contributes significantly to road safety and ITS applications. Ebenezer presented his research at the 39th Canadian Conference on Artificial Intelligence (Canadian AI 2026).

title: VIDLab Team Presents at Canadian AI 2026 and CRV 2026
summary: Congratulations to our VIDLab team members who attended and presented their research at the 39th Canadian Conference on Artificial Intelligence (Canadian AI) and the 23rd Conference on Robots and Vision (CRV) 2026, held at Simon Fraser University, Vancouver.
content:
Congratulations to Our Students on Outstanding Presentations at Canadian AI 2026 and CRV 2026!

We are immensely proud to celebrate the exceptional achievements of our VIDLab students who presented their cutting-edge research at the 39th Canadian Conference on Artificial Intelligence (Canadian AI 2026) and the 23rd Conference on Robots and Vision (CRV 2026), held May 23-29, 2026, at Simon Fraser University in Vancouver, BC, Canada.

These prestigious national conferences brought together leading researchers, scholars, and practitioners in artificial intelligence, computer vision, and robotics from across Canada and internationally. Our students demonstrated remarkable research excellence and represented VIDLab with distinction.

Congratulations to our outstanding presenters:

  • Gaeul Han presented at Canadian AI 2026:
    'Enhancing Thermal Image Object Detection using Spatial Edge-aware Attention'
    This innovative work showcases advanced techniques in thermal imaging and object detection for autonomous driving applications.
  • Ebenezer Penoo presented at Canadian AI 2026:
    'Attention Gated Bidirectional LSTM for Real-time Rear-end Collision Prediction in ITS'
    This research contributes to intelligent transportation systems and road safety through advanced deep learning methods.
  • Thenukan Pathmanathan presented two papers at CRV 2026:
    'xModel-KD: Cross-modal Knowledge Distillation for 3D Scene Perception using LiDAR' (Poster)
    This work demonstrates innovation in cross-modal learning and knowledge distillation for 3D scene understanding using LiDAR point clouds.
    'ConTrans: Learning Text-enhanced Local-global Temporal Representations for Zero-shot Temporal Action Localization'
    This research advances video understanding through text-enhanced temporal representations for zero-shot action localization.

The team was accompanied by Dr. Thangarajah Akilan, who provided invaluable guidance and mentorship throughout the conference. The event offered exceptional opportunities for professional networking, collaborative discussions, and exposure to the latest advances in AI and computer vision research.

This remarkable accomplishment reflects the dedication, hard work, and research excellence that defines VIDLab. We are incredibly proud of our students for their outstanding contributions to the field and for representing our lab with such distinction on this national platform.

title: Congratulations to Our 2025 Graduates at Lakehead University Convocation
summary: VIDLab celebrates the academic achievements of Christopher Silver, Nusrat Jahan, Tharrengini Suresh, and Harish Sundaralingam who attended the Spring 2025 Convocation ceremony at Lakehead University.
content:
Lakehead University Spring 2025 Convocation Ceremony - Thunder Bay Campus

Celebrating Academic Excellence and Research Achievements!

We are incredibly proud to congratulate our outstanding graduates Christopher Silver, Nusrat Jahan, Tharrengini Suresh, and Harish Sundaralingam who participated in Lakehead University's Spring 2025 Convocation ceremonies. Their dedication to research and academic excellence exemplifies the high standards of VIDLab.

The Spring 2025 Convocation ceremonies at Lakehead University's Thunder Bay campus took place from May 29-30, 2025, celebrating the achievements of graduating students across all faculties. Our graduates participated in multiple ceremony sessions, with each ceremony running approximately 2.5 hours and followed by receptions at the campus surrounding Lake Tamblyn and inside the Agora (University Centre).

Dr. Akilan commented: 'Watching our students achieve their academic milestones is one of the most rewarding aspects of leading VIDLab. Christopher, Nusrat, Tharrengini, and Harish have demonstrated exceptional research capabilities and dedication. Their work in areas ranging from semantic segmentation to object detection will have lasting impact on the field.'

Graduate Achievements:

  • Christopher Silver: Completed his MSc in Electrical and Computer Engineering with research focus on advanced computer vision algorithms and deep learning applications
  • Nusrat Jahan: Completed her MSc in Electrical and Computer Engineering with research focus on 'An Improved Semi-Supervised Learning Framework for Image Semantic Segmentation'
  • Tharrengini Suresh: Graduated with distinction with her MSc in Electrical and Computer Engineering, contributing to 'Semantic Segmentation with Edge-Context Enrichment and Attention Strategies: A Refined Framework for Improved Performance in Complex Visual Environments'
  • Harish Sundaralingam: Achieved his MSc in Electrical and Computer Engineering, specializing in 'Enhancing Object Detection in Complex Scenes: A Semantic Segmentation-aware Framework with Attention-Gating for Improved Small Object Detection'
Left: Nusrat Jahan, Right: Christopher Silver
Tharrengini Suresh
Harish Sundaralingam

The Thunder Bay convocation ceremonies were held at Lakehead University's campus (955 Oliver Road), with graduates from the Faculty of Natural Resources Management, Faculty of Science and Environmental Studies, and Faculty of Social Sciences and Humanities participating in the May 30th morning ceremony. Each ceremony provided an exceptional opportunity for graduates to join their classmates and professors in celebrating their accomplishments at Lakehead.

We wish our graduates continued success in their future endeavors and look forward to their continued contributions to the field of intelligent systems and data analytics.
